correctness.rationale: Exact invariance follows by a checked rational factor identity and a uniform tropical logarithmic limit. The eight affine facets yield the explicit seven-vertex polygon for every h>3; determinant-one branches preserve primitive arclength, while orientation and the image P0→P3 give a true circle translation by 3h-5. Coprimality with perimeter 5k-8 proves one orbit on each integer shell k>=4; the k=3 integer seven-cycle is separately enumerated. Area and twist follow by shoelace and differentiation. Standalone SymPy and exact Fraction tests reproduce 441 boundary samples and complete shells through k=200, but infinity is proved analytically, not inferred from samples.

Full texts of the closest autonomous max and max-plus sources use mathematically different maps; nonautonomous max-type literature remains a disclosed priority risk. Statement/implication comparisons, not keyword absence, support a qualified originality pass.
residual_risks: The full 1998 Grove–Kent–Ladas article was inaccessible; an exact alternating max map computation in it would affect originality.
Unindexed or unpublished equivalent two-periodic max-map conjugacies could prove an implication not found in the inspected sources.
A formal identity between reparameterized circle rotation fractions does not establish a plane or integer-lattice conjugacy; no novelty claim is based solely on differing displayed fractions.

value.rationale: Minimal periodic forcing is a natural dynamical extension of classic Lyness max and rational two-season maps. The theorem simultaneously answers the motivated outer-circle rigidity/rotation question, the exact integer energy-shell orbit multiplicity question, and the central-boundary exception. The global transitivity for every lattice initial state, with periods unbounded and explicit 5k-8 growth, is not a textbook substitution or an arbitrary finite case and may serve as a precise comparison benchmark for periodically forced piecewise-integrable maps.
